method: Fresh auditors read SPEC_V2 section by section against the tree in four waves; every evidence quote is the raw line at the cited path and is re-verified by scripts/verify-findings.py before admission.

findings.title: Gate evidence is caller-opt-in, not required
findings.problem: require_evidence defaults false and is supplied per call; no gate/policy declares evidence mandatory, and a no-evidence gate records no override, so the refusal/override/metric rule does not exist.
findings.failure_scenario: pm.route_gate 'deploy' with evidence [] and require_evidence omitted opens an approvable gate; work ships with no artefact or run judged.
findings.acceptance: Empty evidence returns 422 gate_evidence_missing; a waiver is accepted only when approval_policy declares it, is stored on the approval, and increments the override metric read by the governance audit.

resolved_by.evidence: cargo test -p conveyor-actions --test spine_gates: 11 passed; also a_gate_with_evidence_opens, an_explicit_evidence_waiver_is_recorded

findings.title: WBS nodes accepted on a checkbox
findings.problem: wbs.update validates status only against the enum, then writes acceptance/evidence verbatim; an empty evidence array is legal.

evidence.quote: status = coalesce($6, status), acceptance = coalesce($7, acceptance),

findings.failure_scenario: PATCH status=accepted, evidence=[] marks a work package accepted although no run or artefact meets its criteria.
findings.acceptance: Accepting with evidence [] returns 422 wbs_acceptance_evidence_missing unless an approved approval row cites run/artefact evidence for each criterion.

resolved_by.evidence: cargo test -p conveyor-actions --test plan_spine: 14 passed

findings.title: Change requests may carry an empty impact block
findings.problem: validate_change only rejects null; {} passes and the DB CHECK only tests key presence, so no scope/schedule/cost/risk impact analysis is required.
findings.failure_scenario: A change is inserted with meta.impact {}; the approver sees no scope, schedule, cost or risk delta yet can advance the baseline.
findings.acceptance: Inserting kind='change' with an impact lacking any of scope/schedule/cost/risk returns 422 change_impact_missing, enforced in the store and the DB constraint.

resolved_by.evidence: spine_gates 17/17. `a_change_with_no_impact_analysis_is_refused`: a change created with `meta.impact` `{}` is refused 422 change_impact_missing and writes no row, a raw INSERT bypassing the store is refused by the 0065 CHECK, and the same change with a `scope` delta is created 201; `a_change_impact_cannot_be_stripped_by_an_update`: an update replacing `meta` with `impact: {}` is refused 422 and neither meta nor version moves. `validate_change` requires a JSON object with at least one non-null scope/schedule/cost/risk key; `changes.request` now takes that typed block instead of an integer.

findings.title: Post-baseline scope edits bypass change control
findings.problem: Post-baseline scope edits bypass change control: the baseline action itself is guarded, but a direct wbs.update after the baseline never consults the baseline or a change_id.
findings.failure_scenario: After the scope baseline is approved, WBS titles/body/inputs are edited; no change row exists and runs execute against unpinned scope.
findings.acceptance: After an approved baseline, WBS mutations return 409 rebaseline_requires_change unless an approved kind='change' references that baseline with an impact block.

resolved_by.evidence: plan_spine 19/19: after an approved baseline, wbs.create/update/delete return 409 rebaseline_requires_change without an approved kind='change' citing that baseline with an impact block; a project with no baseline is unchanged.

findings.title: Work package to card to run chain is unenforced
findings.problem: wbs_node.card_id and run.card_id are both nullable, and wbs.create cannot set card_id at all, so work packages and runs exist outside the hierarchy.
findings.failure_scenario: A cardless run or an unlinked work_package node is created and executes steps with no path from project to WBS to work package.
findings.acceptance: work_package nodes require card_id and run.card_id is NOT NULL (or the store refuses cardless runs), proven by an insert without the link being refused.

findings.title: Portfolio read model omits in-flight programmes
findings.problem: in_flight_tx selects only FROM project by status, although §5.1 defines the portfolio as every project and programme in flight.

evidence.quote: let sql = "SELECT id, key, name, status, programme_id, version FROM project

findings.failure_scenario: A tenant with an active programme and no active projects sees an empty portfolio; programme work is invisible in the delivery view.
findings.acceptance: portfolio.in_flight returns projects and programmes in the configured in-flight set (an active programme with zero projects appears) and writes no portfolio row.

resolved_by.evidence: plan_spine 19/19: portfolio.in_flight returns a programmes array alongside the unchanged project items; an active programme with zero projects appears and a closed one does not; the action writes no row.

findings.title: Budget enforcement is off by default and no run/binding declares a budget
findings.problem: No migration gives run or job_binding a token/cost budget, and the router gate defaults to Off; even in enforce mode the gate must allow no_active_budget, so an undeclared budget is never refused.

evidence.quote: /// `no_active_budget` — must allow; refusing on them turns a billing blip into an outage.

findings.failure_scenario: An unbudgeted run calls upstream indefinitely; no 429 is ever produced and spend is discovered after the fact.
findings.acceptance: A binding without a budget refuses run start (409/422 naming the missing budget); with a declared budget call N+1 returns 429 budget_exceeded before dispatch and the provider-call counter is unchanged.

resolved_by.evidence: cargo test -p conveyor-actions --test tool_budget: 14 passed (2026-11-21). The router defaults to Enforce; an unbudgeted capturing call is 429 tool_budget_exceeded before dispatch; an internal-agent binding with no ceiling refuses runs.create 422 budget_missing; a priced call records its derived cost on tool_call.

findings.title: Tool spend is a stored column and is absent from every usage roll-up
findings.problem: Tool spend is stored on tool_call and now appears in metrics.usage (tool_calls + tool_cost_usd) and billing.summary, so the 'absent from every roll-up' claim is no longer true. Two halves remain: inference_usage.report is inference-only and carries no tool spend, and both figures sum the stored cost instead of re-deriving it from the ledger at read time (D52).
findings.failure_scenario: Tenant and job spend exclude tool costs, so reported spend and budget utilisation understate actual consumption.
findings.acceptance: The usage report derives tool spend at read time and includes it at tenant and run levels; a priced tool_call appears in both totals in tests.

findings.title: Roll-ups stop at tenant/project/card
findings.problem: metrics.usage now covers the full eight-level metering set (tenant through call), but inference_usage.report still offers only its six inference dimensions (model, caller, prompt and the run/project/card buckets), so a department, programme, job or step question cannot be asked of the inference report.
findings.failure_scenario: The UI cannot show department, programme, job or run-level spend; those panels render empty.
findings.acceptance: The report returns each required level from the ledgers; a test rolls one call up to the job_binding primary department and its programme.

resolved_by.evidence: inference_ 6/6: UsageGroup now carries department, programme, job, run and step (11 dimensions); usage_rows_tx joins run->binding->primary department, run->project->programme, the binding, the run and the step with unattributed fallbacks, and the_extended_dimensions_group_by_programme_job_and_run proves the rows.

findings.title: Attribution joins only run; unattributed calls merge into a project bucket
findings.problem: Aggregation joins only run for project/card; job_binding, department and programme are never joined, and caller_kind='other' is placed in the run's project rather than reported separately.

evidence.quote: LEFT JOIN run r ON r.id = ic.run_id
/// belongs to; a call with no run is the empty bucket, visible rather than dropped.

findings.failure_scenario: Unattributed calls are silently charged to a project/department, and department breakdowns cannot be produced.
findings.acceptance: The report returns an explicit other/unattributed bucket; a caller_kind='other' call is excluded from project totals and counted separately.

resolved_by.evidence: cargo test -p conveyor-store --test inference_ --test metrics_: 5 + 1 passed. An inference_call with caller_kind='other' and a run id appears under 'unattributed' in both the inference usage aggregate and metrics.usage; the project bucket no longer absorbs it.

findings.title: Reconciliation compares conveyor to itself; billing_service is never read
findings.problem: #46 redefines billing.summary as conveyor's own derived ledger, and metrics.reconcile consumes that caller-supplied figure, so no external charging-system roll-up is compared.

evidence.quote: /// V1 read this from a separate Python billing service. #46 (owner, 2026-11-16) ruled billing is

findings.failure_scenario: Charges diverge from billing_service, yet reconciliation reports exact because it compares the ledger to itself.
findings.acceptance: reconcile reads billing_service's tenant×day×project×actor×app×provider×model roll-up via the declared action; a test where it differs from conveyor opens an incident card.

findings.title: Unpriced calls become zero in the billing/reconciliation figure
findings.problem: BillingSummaryOut carries no unpriced count; unpriced calls contribute zero to total_usd, the figure reconcile compares, so a false exact match hides unmeasured spend. No Portfolio/Organisation panel consumes usage data.
findings.failure_scenario: An unpriced model renders as free in tenant and billing totals, and reconciliation passes while spend is hidden.
findings.acceptance: billing.summary and reconcile expose unpriced_calls and refuse an exact verdict when it is greater than zero; a snapshot test asserts the count is present.

findings.title: Phase gates are vacuous without a hand-authored profile, and the caller may choose a draft profile
findings.problem: advance_phase_tx reads only adm_profile.artifact_requirements and adm_profile.contract_kinds; the standard's artifact_type.mandatory rows are never consulted. A phase key absent from the profile yields an empty set, which is treated as satisfied, and a contract kind is required only when the profile maps the phase to a string other than none. phases_advance accepts a client-supplied profile_key, and get_profile_tx resolves a named profile regardless of its status.

evidence.quote: AND (($2::text IS NOT NULL AND key = $2) OR $2::text IS NULL)

findings.failure_scenario: An actor creates profile x with artifact_requirements {} and contract_kinds {}, then calls architecture.phases_advance with profile_key x; every phase from preliminary through h closes with no artefacts, no SAW and no contract.
findings.acceptance: phases_advance returns 409 missing_mandatory when the phase set is absent/empty/malformed; profile keys and values must validate against artifact_type keys and the four contract kinds; a profile_key that is not board-adopted is refused; add a test closing phase A with an empty profile and expect 409.

resolved_by.evidence: also a_draft_profile_cannot_govern_the_gate; togaf_profile_gates green

findings.title: Phase G is not a gate: no contract/review required at design or phase advance, and programme-track projects skip it
findings.problem: Phase G is not a gate: only H is special-cased. A non-programme project's contract, review and waiver checks run only at close, after the work; g requires a live contract only when the profile maps g to a contract kind, and review or waiver never gate g.
findings.failure_scenario: A delivery project of track programme (or any delivery before closure) advances phase g and passes design with neither a live delivery contract nor a compliance review; a non_conformant review without waiver is likewise never blocking until close.
findings.acceptance: phases_advance(g) returns 409 unless a review exists on a live delivery contract for the project and, when level is non_conformant, an active unexpired waiver exists; the design gate action performs the same checks without the track exemption; tests cover programme track.

resolved_by.evidence: also crates/actions/tests/togaf_close_gate.rs::a_programme_track_project_is_not_exempt_from_phase_g

findings.title: Board-adopted ADM profile can be rewritten after adoption and adoption cites an unvalidated decision
findings.problem: profile_tailor upserts on (tenant,key) and updates artifact_requirements/contract_kinds on a row whose status is adopted, with no re-adoption; the WHERE clause only excludes retired. adopt_profile_tx writes any board_decision_id with no check that it is an approved architecture_board decision about this profile, and the column has no FK.
findings.failure_scenario: After adoption, an actor tailors the same profile to remove phase A artefacts and contract kinds, weakening every subsequent gate without any board decision; a draft profile is adopted citing a random uuid.
findings.acceptance: Tailoring an adopted profile either returns 409 or resets status to draft requiring re-adoption; adopt_profile_tx requires an approved architecture_board approval whose meta identifies this profile; FK or EXISTS check added, with tests.

resolved_by.evidence: also adoption_requires_an_approved_decision_about_this_profile

findings.title: A draft Architecture Board can govern, and can be approved with an empty charter
findings.problem: decide_board_tx verifies only that the body row exists, then inserts an architecture_board approval for any subject, including a delivery contract, without requiring the body's status to be active. Only a board-subject approval activates a draft body. Contract approval checks the approval row's gate/status but not the body behind it. Charter, commissioning authority and members default to empty.

evidence.quote: "gate": "an architecture project passes Preliminary and A–F with each phase's mandatory artefacts approved and its contract live; a phase missing a mandatory artefact is refused; a delivery project without a live contract is refused at design; a compliance review records one level and a waiver names its owner and review date; an H review produces exactly one change or kata",

findings.failure_scenario: A draft, never-approved governance_body issues an approved architecture_board decision for a delivery contract; contracts_approve accepts it and the contract goes live under a board with empty charter and no members.
findings.acceptance: decide_board_tx returns 409 unless body status is active, except a subject_kind board self-approval; board approval refuses empty charter/commissioning_authority/members; contract approval resolves body_id from approval meta and requires active status; tests added.

findings.title: Untyped, unprojected artefacts and links with no tenant/project consistency
findings.problem: artifacts_create accepts project_id and artifact_type_id as null, so artefacts exist outside the standard and outside any project; the phase gate joins artifact_type and can never count them. link_artifacts_tx inserts from/to ids with only existence FKs, no join proving both artefacts share a tenant or project.
findings.failure_scenario: A client creates an artefact with null type and project (invisible to every gate), then links two artefacts from different projects or tenants; the repository reports a trace edge that crosses governance boundaries.
findings.acceptance: artifacts_create requires non-null project_id and artifact_type_id (422 otherwise); link_artifacts_tx refuses when from/to differ in tenant or project, implemented as a JOIN in the INSERT/SELECT and covered by cross-tenant and cross-project tests.

findings.title: Phase H enforces existence, not exactly one typed outcome
findings.problem: The H gate asks whether any compliance review in the project has a non-null outcome. Uniqueness is per (project, contract), so a project with two delivery contracts can record two typed outcomes, and an outcome attached to a phase-G review satisfies H.

evidence.quote: WHERE tenant_id = $1 AND project_id = $2 AND outcome IS NOT NULL
ON CONFLICT (tenant_id, project_id, contract_id) DO NOTHING
WHERE tenant_id = $1 AND project_id = $2 AND outcome IS NOT NULL

findings.failure_scenario: Two contracts each record a change outcome, or a G review carries an outcome; phase h advances with two typed outcomes, so the change/kata decision is ambiguous.
findings.acceptance: H advance returns 409 unless exactly one review row with an outcome exists for the project and that review belongs to a live delivery contract; a second outcome row is refused by constraint; tests cover zero, two and G-attached outcomes.

findings.title: Tranche authorisation is asserted by the seed, not earned by a review
findings.problem: The seed inserts tranches with a state but no authorisation_review_id (tranche 1 is seeded authorised), and the start gate accepts authorised/in_review/closed without ever checking a review exists. The review evidence check accepts any non-null, non-empty-array value for three free-text keys, so baselines, benefit status and risk register need not reference rows.

evidence.quote: (tenant_id, programme_id, number, state, entry_criteria, exit_criteria, review_at)

findings.failure_scenario: A fresh tenant seeds tranche 1 as authorised with no programme_tranche_review; every tranche-1 project passes assert_project_tranche_authorised_tx and starts. A reviewer can submit evidence {"baselines":"none","benefit_status":"none","risk_register":"none"} and the continue/pause/stop gate records it.
findings.acceptance: A start gate refuses any tranche whose authorisation_review_id is NULL; evidence must cite existing baseline, benefit-status and risk-register row ids; seeded authorised/closed tranches carry a review row or are refused.

findings.title: Benefit measurement is presence-only and realized needs only two timestamps
findings.problem: Completeness now rejects empty/whitespace/placeholder baselines and targets and a realized status now needs non-empty transition evidence in addition to both timestamps. What remains missing is the measurement VALUES: benefit_transition stores timestamps plus a free-form readiness document, so a realized claim still has no typed baseline/post value to compare. The seeded B1-B6 baselines bypass the store with raw SQL (see v1-p83-3).

evidence.quote: /// The editable fields of a realization record. `None` leaves the stored value in place.

findings.failure_scenario: benefits.transition_upsert accepts baseline_measured_at and post_measured_at with evidence [], then benefits.update sets status realized. No post-transition measurement exists, yet the benefit claims improvement.
findings.acceptance: Completeness rejects empty/whitespace/non-measurement baselines and targets; realized requires a transition with baseline and post measurement values plus evidence, not timestamps alone.

findings.title: BCM and benefit ownership are free text, not job_keys
findings.problem: No SRO, BCM, sponsoring-group or board job_key is seeded. The seed writes owner_role into operational_area and omits owner_job_id and benefit_owner_job_id, bypassing insert_benefit_tx. All six seeded benefits therefore have no job owner; benefits.update then refuses them as benefit_owner incomplete.
findings.failure_scenario: The programme's benefits are owned by the string "BCM"; any job or no job can own a benefit through the action path, and the seeded rows cannot be edited because benefit_owner_job_id is NULL.
findings.acceptance: Roles are seeded as job_keys; benefit_owner_job_id must resolve to the BCM job; the seed uses insert_benefit_tx or supplies a real job id.

findings.title: Programme baselines can be taken and approved but no gate requires them
findings.problem: programme_tranche.baseline_ref is nullable and update_tranche_tx only checks that a cited baseline exists, never that it is approved or which of management/governance/boundary it is. Tranche review evidence mentions baselines as free text, so an authorised tranche can cite nothing or an unapproved row.

evidence.quote: "SELECT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM programme_baseline WHERE tenant_id = $1 AND id = $2)",

findings.failure_scenario: A tranche with baseline_ref NULL is reviewed continue and authorises the next tranche; alternatively it cites an unapproved management baseline. The management/governance/boundary trio is never recorded against the work it governs.
findings.acceptance: A tranche cannot be authorised without cited baselines of the required kinds, each approved_by set; review evidence resolves to those ids.

findings.title: Closure bypasses the closure review and the realisation plan
findings.problem: Closure bypasses the closure review and the realisation plan: close_programme_tx now refuses a missing plan and an ownerless plan, but programmes.update writes any status unchecked and the transaction checks no review, so the update path still closes a programme without either gate.

evidence.quote: "UPDATE programme SET status = 'closed', version = version + 1, updated_at = now()

findings.failure_scenario: A project with no outputs closes with neither approval nor closure record; the programme closes on a draft plan whose only post-closure content is the owner string.
findings.acceptance: Every close requires an approved closure asset and gate; programme close requires an approved, published realisation plan naming measured post-closure ownership (a job), not free text.

findings.title: PMP enforcement is partial: closure requires only the scope baseline
findings.problem: Closure reads the approved scope baseline only. Schedule and cost baselines are never required, no WBS node is required for execution or closure, and the risk/issue/assumption/dependency registers need not be non-empty. Those artefacts exist as tables and actions but are not gated.
findings.failure_scenario: A programme project closes with an empty WBS, no schedule/cost baseline and empty registers, provided its charter and scope baseline exist.
findings.acceptance: Closure refuses unless approved scope, schedule and cost baselines exist, at least one accepted WBS deliverable exists, and the register kinds required by the project's standard are populated.

findings.title: Coach remedies are recorded, never applied
findings.problem: coach.remedy validates the closed set, inserts a coach_remedy row, marks the interruption remedied and returns. No consumer reads coach_remedy to retry, move, repull or block anything; the charter's 'apply a bounded remedy' step is a database write only, and the policy retry cap is moot because nothing is ever retried.
findings.failure_scenario: A transient failure is triaged 'retry'; the card sits in the waiting lane, the failed run never reruns, yet the interruption reads 'remedied' and the board shows the block as handled.
findings.acceptance: coach.remedy dispatches the derived remedy through real actions (process_runs.start for retry, cards.move, repull trigger, block) and stores the resulting run/effect id; a test asserts the run or card actually changed.

resolved_by.evidence: cargo test -p conveyor-actions --test coach: 20 passed; also a_remedy_whose_effect_fails_is_not_marked_remedied

findings.title: Systemic finding terminates at a process-run id; no development project, measurement or adoption gate
findings.problem: The systemic path's whole effect is starting process key kata.open and storing its run id as kata_candidate_id. There is no kata record naming an instrument and threshold, no tenant-kata scoping, no kata-candidate trigger that opens a development project or config change, and no measurement or mandatory adoption approval anywhere in the loop.
findings.failure_scenario: A postmortem or systemic triage marks the finding 'systemic'; a kata run appears, nothing else. The candidate change is never built, measured on held-out data, or gated for adoption, so production never changes.
findings.acceptance: A systemic finding opens a kata with named instrument and success threshold under the kata tenant; a kata candidate opens a development project or config-change path; measurement and a dual-control adoption approval block production until granted; tests exercise the full chain.

resolved_by.evidence: The coach policy declares a kata pin (instrument_kind/id/version, held-out split + sha256, pre-registered prediction, base_ref) and the coach opens the kata rows through the kata capability with the interruption signature (coach.rs::a_systemic_class_opens_one_measured_kata asserts the kata row, its signature and instrument version, no documentation run). A policy without a complete pin escalates through a coach.kata gate and opens no kata (::a_systemic_class_without_a_pinned_instrument_escalates). Measurement and dual-control adoption the path hands to are proved in crates/actions/tests/kata_gate.rs::only_the_held_out_split_on_the_pinned_version_measures, ::adoption_needs_another_person_and_a_measured_candidate and ::the_kata_measurer_cannot_decide_its_adoption. cargo test -p conveyor-actions --test coach: 22 passed.

findings.title: Rework rate is not computed anywhere
findings.problem: The quality family requires rework rate from run/approval/eval rows. metrics.flow and evidence_tx expose only approvals, run totals, benefits and flow figures; FlowOut has no rework or first-pass-yield field, and rework is not even listed as unavailable. No rework computation exists in crates or apps.
findings.failure_scenario: An operator asking Measure for rework rate cannot get the figure at all, so first-pass yield and rework improvement claims are unverifiable.
findings.acceptance: A read-time rework-rate derivation over run/approval rows is exposed by the metrics family (or declared unavailable with a real reason); unit/integration test asserts the arithmetic.

findings.title: Interruptions are silently dropped: per-card cap and live-run skip
findings.problem: The cap counts every interruption on a card regardless of signature and refuses the fourth failed run, which then gets no coach card and no escalation. err.card also suppresses coaching whenever any live root run exists on the card. §6.2 only permits folding/refusing a repeat of the same signature inside its window.
findings.failure_scenario: A card fails four times with four distinct defects; the fourth failure is logged and commented but never triaged, so a real interruption has no card and no owner.
findings.acceptance: Every failed-run interruption either creates exactly one coach card or escalates/folds under the (card_id, signature) rule; a distinct signature is never suppressed by a card-level count or an unrelated live run.

resolved_by.evidence: The per-card breadth cap and the live-run skip are removed from err.card and coach.interrupt; a fourth DISTINCT signature opens exactly one coach card (the test drives three distinct interruptions then a fourth and asserts the card, the run and four recorded interruptions), and the repeat signature still escalates (crates/actions/tests/coach.rs::a_repeat_signature_escalates_instead_of_a_second_card). Suites: coach 21 passed, computed_set 11 passed.

findings.title: Coach is wired only to failed runs
findings.problem: coach.interrupt has one caller: err.card on a failed run. WIP breaches, stale leases, gate timeouts and board events, all named charter inputs, have no producer that opens an interruption or coach card, so flow protection is reactive to crashes only.

evidence.quote: // (c) The coach, through the one admission path (T4). `coach.interrupt` creates the coach
alert / failed run / eval delta / prompt finding / coach escalation

findings.failure_scenario: A board exceeds its WIP limit or a lease goes stale for days; no interruption, triage or remedy exists, and the Measure views show the block only after a downstream failure.
findings.acceptance: Each §6.2 input kind (WIP breach, stale lease, gate timeout, board event) invokes coach.interrupt through a tested producer carrying its own signature.

findings.title: Orphan coach cards can be created by the public create path
findings.problem: cards.create accepts any catalogue card type, including coach, and validates neither an interruption row nor the meta.interrupted_card_id it is handed. Only coach.interrupt is supposed to mint coach cards; a direct caller can create one with no interruption backing it.
findings.failure_scenario: A caller with cards:write creates a coach card naming an arbitrary or nonexistent interrupted_card_id; the board shows a coach card with no triage, remedy or escalation and no row to audit.
findings.acceptance: Card type coach is refused on the public create path, or coach cards must be created atomically with an interruption referencing them; a test proves an orphan is impossible.

resolved_by.evidence: cards.create refuses the coach card type unless the internal, serde-skipped flag set only by coach.interrupt is present; the public path (dev:alice) gets 422 coach_card_internal and the board holds zero coach cards, while coach.interrupt still creates its card with the interruption in the same transaction.

findings.title: PI plan auto-materialises with no human approval
findings.problem: materialise_pi_tx creates cards and sets the cadence to materialised in one transaction; no approver, approval row or approval_target gates materialisation, and the scheduler calls it unattended.

evidence.quote: SET state = 'materialised', version = version + 1, updated_at = now(),

findings.failure_scenario: An unattended tick commits an unapproved plan, with unvalidated WSJF inputs, as materialised work.
findings.acceptance: Materialisation stops at awaiting_approval; a named human approval is required before cards count as planned and the tick cannot bypass it.

resolved_by.evidence: cargo test -p conveyor-actions --test pi_plan_approval: 8 passed. A pending or rejected plan materialises nothing; an approved plan materialises exactly once inside the WIP slots; a service principal's decision cannot approve a plan.

findings.title: programme_cadence state machine unenforced
findings.problem: state is an unconstrained text column and cadences.update writes input.state verbatim; no CHECK, transition table or guard refuses illegal jumps.
findings.failure_scenario: A caller moves planned directly to closed, or persists an arbitrary string, destroying cadence history.
findings.acceptance: The five states are CHECKed and disallowed transitions are refused with 409 and covered by tests.

resolved_by.evidence: programme_cadence 5/5: migration 0064 CHECKs the state to the six values the code writes; cadence_move is consulted by the edit path, the approval gate and the materialiser, and an illegal jump is 409 cadence_illegal_transition. The CHECK was verified against a throwaway postgres:18.

findings.title: Programme/ART has no shared_config and no computed portfolio view
findings.problem: programme is a flat row (name/status/owner); grep finds no shared_config in crates, apps or migrations, and no CREATE VIEW exists though §8.2 requires shared, locked ART config.
findings.failure_scenario: Every project re-declares cadence/ART config; nothing inherits or locks it, so programmes drift.
findings.acceptance: programme.shared_config exists with inheritance/lock semantics, resolved on read, and tests prove a locked value cannot be overridden per project.

resolved_by.evidence: programme_shared_config 3 passed on the merged lane: migration 0068 adds the column and its shape CHECK; programmes.create/update/get/list carry shared_config; resolve_shared_config makes a locked programme key win over a project override; a flat object reads as values with no locks; a round trip through the programme row preserves the config. The migration-set test expects 68 and --check-lock passes after the lock was regenerated.

findings.title: Backlog refinement is a dead cadence kind
findings.problem: kind='refinement' is accepted at creation, but the only scheduled pass processes pi, demo and retro; no refinement job re-scores WSJF or flags stale items.

evidence.quote: WHERE tenant_id = $1 AND kind IN ('demo', 'retro') AND state = 'planned'

findings.title: The L3 human gate on a generated draft is forgeable by any service principal, and any accepted non-rule decision on the card qualifies
findings.problem: §7.1 makes L3 a human approval (approval + approval_decision) for every irreversible action, and §7.4 says a generated draft becomes applicable only through an action with a gate. ladder.record accepts rung='human' from any caller holding governance:write (the action is kind=internal) and copies ctx.actor_kind with no check that the actor is a person; record_decision_tx only checks that the cited approval row exists in the tenant, never that its approval_decision is accepted or that it covers this draft. ladder.apply_draft then admits any accepted non-rule decision that names the same card, regardless of the question it answered or the artefact it was about, so a routine accepted laya classification also unlocks a generated patch.

It then calls ladder.apply_draft for the generated code patch; the check passes because the decision is not a rule, is 'accepted', and names the card. No person approved anything. Separately, an accepted laya decision for request.classify on the card is enough to apply any draft, so the draft is never gated on the decision that actually reviewed it.
findings.acceptance: ladder.record refuses rung='human' unless the actor is a person and the cited approval has an accepted approval_decision bound to this decision; ladder.apply_draft requires an accepted decision of a dedicated draft-application gate kind (and/or the document's prompt_sha256/inference_call_id) and refuses a generic or pending approval; tests prove a pending approval and an unrelated accepted laya decision both cannot gate a draft.

findings.title: L1 laya is never invoked: ladder.evaluate stamps rung=laya on caller-supplied answer, confidence and latency
findings.problem: §7.2 defines the laya contract (POST /v1/systemone over row-authored questions) and §7.3 makes laya mandatory for the listed decisions. The repository contains no ladder laya client: the only laya HTTP path is process/step.rs's judge. ladder.evaluate instead takes the answer, confidence, probabilities and latency from the request body and writes rung='laya' with whatever configuration versions happen to be resolved. The 'calibrated choice' is therefore an unverifiable assertion; nothing distinguishes a real laya answer from a number an agent invented.

The ledger records a laya decision with full policy/refinement/laya-config pins and empty probabilities, indistinguishable from a genuine calibrated response. Because nothing compares the row to a systemone response, a fabricated confidence can clear any threshold, and the 'L1 before L2' ordering the chapter depends on is not evidence-backed.

findings.title: Options are inline request text, not authored/versioned rows, and the answer is never checked against them
findings.problem: §7.2 requires options to be authored and versioned rows (decision_option) and never free text from a prompt, so a choice is provably one of a finite set. In the ladder surfaces, options arrive in the same request body as the answer, the option-set version is fabricated as 1 whenever any options are supplied, and record_decision_tx inserts the options after the decision without comparing new.answer to any option key. A laya decision can therefore carry an answer outside its own recorded option set, or a one-element option set that merely echoes the answer.

evidence.quote: "INSERT INTO decision_option (tenant_id, decision_id, key, label, payload)

findings.failure_scenario: A prompt or agent sends options [{key:'yes'},{key:'no'}] with answer 'yes, because the ticket says so'. The row stores option_set_version=1 and two option rows, and the answer is accepted as a valid laya choice even though it is not a key in the set. Conversely it can send only the option it picked, so the ledger can never prove the decision was constrained to a finite authored set; a prompt can inject or shrink the option space per call.
findings.acceptance: option sets are authored/versioned rows resolved by policy+question, the evaluate action references the set (and a real version), and the answer must equal one of that set's keys or the action returns 422; tests cover an answer outside the set and a caller trying to pass its own option list.

resolved_by.evidence: Option sets are authored and versioned rows (`decision_option_set`/`decision_option_entry`, tenant sets shadowing the library set, refinements pinning `base_hash`), the evaluate action resolves the set by policy+question and pins its real version, and an answer outside the set is refused 422 `answer_not_in_set` with no laya row written. decision_ladder 22/22 at merged head 7b4b9a0: a_tenant_option_set_shadows_the_library_set, a_hidden_option_is_absent_from_the_wire, a_decision_pins_the_option_set_version_it_read, a_caller_cannot_supply_its_own_options, a_refinement_whose_base_changed_is_refused.

findings.title: fail_policy and the Unavailable outcome are stored but never applied; a laya outage cannot become gate_unavailable
findings.problem: §7.2 requires Unavailable to be gate_unavailable, following fail_policy, and never silently a pass. The domain's unavailable() maps closed|open to refused|action, but nothing calls it: ladder.evaluate requires a confidence, computes only the threshold outcome, and the sole caller of effective.fail_policy() is validate_vocabulary(). The fail_policy column is validated for spelling and then dead at the evaluation boundary, so a closed safety policy and an open routing policy behave identically when laya is unreachable.

evidence.quote: pub fn unavailable(fail_policy: FailPolicy, action: FailAction) -> Outcome {

findings.failure_scenario: Laya times out during a closed safety-gate pre-check. The caller has no confidence to post, so ladder.evaluate returns 422 confidence_missing and no decision row exists; there is no gate_unavailable, no refused outcome and no escalation record. An operator auditing the run cannot tell whether the gate passed, was skipped, or was never evaluated, and downstream policy can treat the missing row as 'not blocking'.
findings.acceptance: A gate_unavailable path exists on the ladder that records the outage and applies fail_policy (closed => refused, open => the policy action), with a test for an unreachable laya on both a closed and an open policy; open with annotate must record the note, closed must record the refusal.

findings.title: Knowledge-family metrics are explicitly unavailable because the lesson and pack-hit ledgers are absent
findings.problem: §7.5's Knowledge family requires pack hit rate, citation rate, readiness blocks and lesson promotion rate computed from decision, inference_call and lesson rows, and §7.6 requires lesson promotion with >=2 independent evidence references and a person's review. The metrics source row is lesson, which the schema does not have: metrics.flow hard-codes knowledge.lesson_promotion_rate and knowledge.pack_hit_rate into the unavailable list, stating the lesson ledger (T8) is not in the schema and no knowledge-retrieval ledger exists. There is no lesson action module either (knowledge/ has only mod.rs and query.rs).

evidence.quote: reason: "the lesson ledger (T8) is not in the schema".to_owned(),
reason: "no knowledge-retrieval ledger exists; inference_call records the prompt, not the pack hit".to_owned(),

findings.failure_scenario: The Measure panel and the Knowledge family of the metrics API can never report a pack hit rate or a lesson promotion rate, so a tenant cannot tell whether retrieval is helping or whether lessons are being adopted. Because there is no lesson row, the >=2-independent-evidence promotion rule has no enforcement point: a single bad run cannot be promoted through a governed action because there is no action, and when one is added there is no ledger contract for it to check.
findings.acceptance: The lesson ledger (proposed/reviewed/promoted/rejected with evidence references) and a pack-hit source exist; metrics.flow reports real pack_hit_rate and lesson_promotion_rate; promotion refuses fewer than two distinct card/run/incident evidence references or a missing review; tests cover both refusals.

findings.title: A phase missing from the profile advances with zero mandatory artefacts
findings.problem: The gate reads only `profile.artifact_requirements`. When the requested phase has no entry (or an entry that is neither an array nor an object), the set list is empty and `satisfied` is initialised true, so the phase closes with no artefact at all; the `artifact_type.mandatory` column that carries the standard's own mandatory set is seeded and returned but never read by the gate. §8.1 says the mandatory set "comes from the standard, filtered by the tenant's adm_profile" — filtered, not replaced.
findings.failure_scenario: Adopt a profile that names requirements only for the phases walked so far (`artifact_requirements: {"preliminary": [...], "a": [...]}`, `contract_kinds: {}`) — the young-capability tailoring §8.1 encourages. Then `architecture.phases_advance {project_id: P, phase_code: "b"}`: sets is empty, satisfied is true, no contract kind is named, and the B node is written `accepted` with evidence `{"artifacts": [], "contract": null}`. Phases B–H can be walked producing nothing although the standard marks Business Service/Function, Data Entity Catalog, Technology Standards and the rest mandatory.
findings.acceptance: A phase with no explicit profile entry falls back to the standard's mandatory artifact_type set for that phase/plateau (or the profile is refused as un-tailored at adoption); advancing B with no approved Business Service/Function is refused by architecture_artifact_missing.

resolved_by.evidence: also a_draft_profile_cannot_govern_the_gate; mandatory_sets_tx joins artifact_type.mandatory

findings.title: Profile adoption accepts any UUID as its board decision
findings.problem: `adopt_profile_tx` writes the caller's `adopt_with_decision_id` into board_decision_id with no existence, gate, status or subject check, and `migrations/0054_architecture.sql` gives the column no foreign key to `approval` (contrast architecture_contract_approval_fk). The same codebase validates exactly this for contracts in `architecture.contracts_approve` (gate = architecture_board, status = approved, subject = this contract). §8.1's Preliminary gate is "the board adopts the profile"; here the gate is a client-supplied string.
findings.failure_scenario: Call `architecture.profile_tailor {key: "default", name: "Default", phase_set: [...], artifact_requirements: {...}, contract_kinds: {...}, adopt_with_decision_id: "<any random uuid>"}`. The profile returns 200 with status 'adopted' and no approval row exists anywhere in the tenant. The recorded capability baseline now claims board adoption, and every later phase gate runs against a profile whose adoption decision cannot be produced.
findings.acceptance: Adoption refuses unless the id names an approval row with gate='architecture_board', status='approved', subject_kind='adm_profile' and subject_id = this profile id; the migration carries the FK and a NOT NULL board_decision_id for status='adopted'.

findings.title: contracts_request retires another project's live contract via supersedes_id
findings.problem: `request_contract_tx` retires the row named by `supersedes_id` with an UPDATE scoped by tenant only — never by project, kind or phase — and then writes `superseded_by_id` on it unconditionally. Any contract id of the tenant is accepted, so a request for one project can retire the governing contract of another.

evidence.quote: WHERE tenant_id = $1 AND id = $2 AND status IN ('draft', 'live')",

findings.failure_scenario: Project P2 holds its live delivery_contract C2. A caller issues `architecture.contracts_request {project_id: P1, kind: "statement_of_architecture_work", phase_code: "a", title: "SAW", supersedes_id: C2}`. C2 flips to status='superseded' and its superseded_by_id now points at P1's SAW. P2's close gate then answers closure_contract_missing and `architecture.phases_advance` on G answers architecture_contract_not_live — two gates broken by a write to a different project.
findings.acceptance: A superseded contract must belong to the same project (and kind/phase) as the new one, else 409; a failed check writes neither the retirement nor the new row.

findings.title: phase_progress reports a phase evidenced by draft artefacts and superseded contracts
findings.problem: `phase_progress` builds `artifact_phases` from every architecture_artifact row the snapshot carries without testing `status`, and picks one contract per (project, phase) by recency without testing `status`; "evidenced" is then computed from those sets. The console therefore reports progress under a rule that contradicts `advance_phase_tx`, which only accepts an `approved` artefact and a `live` contract.
findings.failure_scenario: Create one artefact with `phase_code: "c"` and leave it in `draft` (or supersede an approved one), then read the snapshot: the project's phase_progress marks C `state: "evidenced"` and `next_required` moves to D, while `architecture.phases_advance {phase_code: "c"}` returns 409 architecture_artifact_missing. The Architecture destination and the gate disagree about the same phase.
findings.acceptance: phase_progress counts only status='approved' artefacts and status='live' contracts (matching advance_phase_tx), so a phase reported `evidenced` is one the gate would also close.

findings.title: Project start passes when the programme has no tranche row
findings.problem: assert_project_tranche_authorised_tx treats 'no tranche row found' as authorised. project_tranche_state_tx defaults a missing meta.tranche to 1 and returns None when no programme_tranche row has that number; the caller maps None to Ok(()). That None case is meant for standalone projects (programme_id NULL), but it is identical for a programme-bound project whose programme has no tranche rows at all, so the 'no project starts before the first tranche is authorised' rule is not enforced for a fresh programme.
findings.failure_scenario: A programme is created with programmes.create; nobody has created tranche 1 yet. A delivery project is created with programme_id set and meta.tranche=1. projects.create calls assert_project_tranche_authorised_tx, the tranche lookup returns no row, and the gate returns Ok. The project starts work, spends budget and produces outputs before any sponsoring-group tranche review, so the first-tranche authorisation requirement is skipped entirely.
findings.acceptance: For a project whose programme_id is set, a missing tranche row returns 409 tranche_not_authorised (only programme_id NULL may pass); an integration test creates a programme with zero tranches and asserts project start is refused.

resolved_by.evidence: also a_programme_without_a_tranche_plan_keeps_its_legacy_allowance

findings.title: A benefit is accepted with no capability and no operational area
findings.problem: The spec's rule 'Every benefit names the capability it depends on and the operational area that must change' is not enforced. benefits.create defaults capabilities to an empty array and operational_area to the empty string, and the store validation (benefit_profile_missing over BenefitProfileFields) covers only baseline, target, measurement_method and benefit_owner_job_id. Neither capabilities nor operational_area is part of the validated field set on insert or update.
findings.failure_scenario: The BCM registers 'faster onboarding' with a baseline, target, method and owner but leaves capabilities and operational_area empty. benefits.create succeeds (only the four measurement fields are checked). The benefit enters the map with no capability dependency and no operational area to change, and can later be marked realized without any programme capability having been delivered or any part of operations having changed — the exact 'wish' the spec says must be refused.
findings.acceptance: benefits.create and benefits.update refuse 400 benefit_profile_incomplete unless capabilities is a non-empty array and operational_area is non-blank after trim, in addition to the four measurement fields.

resolved_by.evidence: cargo test -p conveyor-actions --test benefit_lifecycle: 13 passed, including a_benefit_without_capabilities_or_an_area_is_refused and a_placeholder_baseline_is_refused (422 benefit_profile_incomplete naming both gaps). spine_msp 10, plan_spine 14 and the parity sample are green with the two fields present.

findings.title: Benefits-map output_ref is free text, so dependency slips miss benefits
findings.problem: benefit_link.output_ref is a plain text column with no foreign key, and benefits.link copies the caller's string unchanged. The store's own contract for record_dependency_slip_tx says the at-risk benefits come from edges where benefit_link.output_ref names a wbs_node id, but no action validates that the string is an existing wbs_node of the programme. The map is therefore accepted with edges that can never participate in a dependency slip.
findings.failure_scenario: The BCM links the benefit to output_ref '3.2.1 Onboarding walkthrough' (a WBS label) instead of the wbs_node UUID. benefits.link accepts it and the map is accepted. When that output's dependency slips, record_dependency_slip_tx matches benefit_link.output_ref against wbs_node ids, finds nothing, and reports zero benefits at risk; the benefit-at-risk metric and the sponsor's escalation both under-report by exactly the benefits the map intended to protect.
findings.acceptance: benefits.link resolves output_ref to an existing wbs_node id in the same programme (refusing a non-uuid or a node from another programme), or the dependency-slip path returns an error when an edge names no node instead of silently returning an empty list.

resolved_by.evidence: plan_spine 17/17 and spine_msp 10/10: a benefit link with a non-UUID output_ref or a node from another programme is 422 benefit_output_unresolved before any row; a node in the benefit's programme is stored as the canonical id; the dependency-slip path now refuses an edge that names no node.

findings.title: Demo and retro cadence rows enforce nothing: no evidence, no credit, no lessons
findings.problem: Demo and retro cadence rows enforce nothing: retros.close now requires a lesson per finding, but cadences.update can close a retro directly and a demo cadence still requires no credit or evidence.
findings.failure_scenario: A PI closes without a system demo. Every deliverable stays accepted because acceptance is a status PATCH (see v2-w2c-4); the retro row exists with empty meta and produces no lesson or kata candidate. The improvement loop the spec says is measured has no rows to measure.
findings.acceptance: A demo cadence refuses to credit/accept a completed deliverable without a typed evidence reference exhibited at that demo, and a retro action writes lessons plus kata candidates linked to the retro cadence row; tests cover the refused credit and the written lessons.

resolved_by.evidence: demo_credit 12 passed / 0 failed and demo_gate 1 passed on the merged lane. Typed evidence is required: a blank, null or empty-object reference is demo_evidence_untyped; an accepted deliverable must carry its evidence. close_retro_tx writes the lesson from the finding's statement and evidence; a systemic finding carries lesson.meta.kata_candidate = {signature,title,rationale,target_ref,prediction:null} and no kata is opened (an unmeasurable kata is never fabricated); cadences.update cannot close a retro — retros.close is the only path.

findings.title: Baseline change guard trusts a self-declared 'approved' status on a register row
findings.problem: `take_baseline_guarded` advances a baseline when the named change row has `status == "approved"`, but `registers.create` and `registers.update` write any status string straight to the row with no validation and no approval gate. Any `portfolio:write` caller can create a change already marked approved, or PATCH an open one, and then re-baseline. The store already has `change_is_approved_tx`, which correctly reads the approval gate, but the baseline guard does not use it.

evidence.quote: /// gate is approved. The approval is the second principal's decision, not the row's status.

findings.failure_scenario: A delivery lead with portfolio:write creates a change row with status 'approved', baseline_ref pointing at the current approved baseline and meta.impact = {}. They then call baselines.take with that change_id. The new baseline is created and cited as advanced by an 'approved' change that no approver ever saw, bypassing §8.4 change control and §8.3's re-baseline rule entirely.
findings.acceptance: The baseline guard resolves approval through the approval table (gate='change', status='approved', meta.change_id matches), not the row status; register create/update refuse status='approved' for change rows (approval is only a gate effect). A test that self-declares approved and re-baselines must be rejected.

resolved_by.evidence: also a_register_cannot_be_born_approved, an_approved_change_gate_advances_the_baseline

findings.title: The trace chain stops at card/project: no run, step, artefact or evidence end
findings.problem: The trace-edge whitelist is governed_asset | card | project. The spec chain continues WBS deliverable → card → run → step → artefact/evidence → acceptance → closure; none of run, step, artefact or evidence is an addressable end, and there is no view action joining them. Gate evidence edges also fire only for evidence items whose kind is governed_asset, so typed run/artefact evidence never leaves an edge at all.
findings.failure_scenario: An auditor asks the governance screen which requirement a given run proves and where its evidence is. trace_links.list can only return requirement→card or requirement→project edges; the run, its steps and its artefacts are unreachable from the requirement, and evidence arrays naming a run are silently skipped by the gate effect. The one question §8.5 says the screen answers cannot be answered.
findings.acceptance: Trace ends include run, step, artefact and evidence (tenant-resolved), and a bounded governance view action returns requirement → cards → runs → steps/artefacts/evidence for a requirement or run; tests build the chain and read it back.

findings.title: Trace links are optional and not required at creation for architecture-governed work
findings.problem: `trace_links.create` is a standalone opt-in action. Work-package/card creation (`wbs.create` and the board path) never checks for a trace link to an approved requirement or architecture asset. The spec requires the link at creation time for architecture-governed work; here it can be added later or never.
findings.failure_scenario: A team starts architecture-governed work (project meta marks it governed), creates the work package and card, and runs it with no requirement/architecture edge. The work is ungoverned and no run can be attributed to an approved requirement; nothing refuses the creation and no report flags the orphan.
findings.acceptance: Creation of a work package/card for an architecture-governed project refuses with 409 unless it carries a trace link to an approved requirement or architecture asset, writing the edge in the same transaction; a test asserts the orphan is refused and the linked creation succeeds.

findings.title: The andon cord can be released by a machine: andon.release never checks that the actor is a person
findings.problem: SPEC §9.2 says the andon cord is released by a person only. andon_release goes straight from the handler context to store::andon::release_tx; it never consults ctx.actor_kind, even though the same crate already uses actor_kind to decide whether an actor is a user (incidents.rs:750). The action is kind="internal", and the invoke boundary's Authority::Internal lane permits any actor_kind that holds the scope (invoke.rs:776), so a scheduled ops job or a coding agent holding andon:write can release a cord a human pulled. The release event records only actor_id, with no principal kind a reader could use to tell a person from a machine.
findings.failure_scenario: At 02:10 a human pulls the cord after a runaway deploy. An automation job (or a coding agent granted andon:write to 'unblock' itself) calls andon.release at 02:12. runs.create stops returning 409 andon-engaged and the worker resumes claiming runs for the tenant, including the pipeline that caused the incident. No human decision exists anywhere in the record, and the released event gives no way to tell the releaser was not a person.
findings.acceptance: andon.release returns 403 unless ctx.actor_kind == "user"; a test asserts a machine principal holding andon:write is refused while a user succeeds, and the andon.released event carries the principal kind.

resolved_by.evidence: andon_release: 4 passed

findings.title: An incident that needed no write can never be postmortemed or resolved, starving the improvement loop
findings.problem: ops.postmortem refuses unless mitigated_at is recorded, and ops.resolve refuses unless both mitigated_at and a postmortem are present. An incident that self-heals, is fixed by a person outside conveyor, or is opened from an alert that then cleared has no mitigation write to run; it therefore can never produce a postmortem, a kata candidate, or a resolution, though §9.2 defines a person-opened incident and a postmortem whose systemic finding should become a kata.

evidence.quote: "a postmortem follows a mitigation; none has been recorded",

findings.failure_scenario: A certificate-expiry alert fires. An operator renews the certificate with their own tooling; conveyor's only write verbs (restart, scale, rollback, flag_flip) are not the fix and running one would be a false record. The incident stays open forever: no postmortem can be written, so the systemic finding (no automated rotation) never becomes a kata, and the card contaminates every open-incidents view and every severity metric.
findings.acceptance: An incident may record mitigation as 'no action required' with a reason (no cluster write, no mitigated write recorded) and may then be postmortemed and resolved; a test asserts a zero-write incident reaches resolved with a postmortem and, when systemic, exactly one kata candidate.

findings.title: The live web shell still exposes only V1's nine destinations; six V2 destinations have no route
findings.problem: apps/web/src/app.rs calls itself the nine-destination shell and its route table plus Sidebar (app.rs:267-322) contain no route or nav entry for Organisation, Authoring, Portfolio, Programme, Plan or Operations; Procedures/Improve exist only as Build sub-screens and an Evals sub-screen. Any deep link to a documented V2 destination falls through to the literal 'No such page.' fallback (app.rs:138). The §10.5 screens therefore cannot be reached in the live product at all.

evidence.quote: V1's nine destinations stand (Today, Board, Runs, Build, Design, Measure, Evals, Govern, Channels). V2 adds:
//! The application root: one boot, then the nine-destination shell.

findings.failure_scenario: The owner or a tenant admin opens /organisation, /portfolio, /programme or /operations (or clicks the destination in a design pack) and the SPA renders 'No such page.'; job catalogue/release administration, tranche reviews, benefits, WBS/baselines and incident/postmortem work have no human surface, so those workflows are API-only in practice.
findings.acceptance: Each §10.5 destination has a live route and Sidebar entry (Organisation, Procedures, Authoring, Portfolio, Programme, Plan, Improve, Operations), each landing on a real screen; or an owner-approved scope cut records the deferral in SPEC_V2 §10.5.

findings.title: The declared authoring.* action family does not exist
findings.problem: SPEC §10.4 declares authoring.intake|draft|review|publish and authoring.assets. The actions crate declares no authoring module (the module inventory spans lib.rs:20-107), and the compile-time registry is exactly the inventory submissions (registry.rs:184); enumeration of all ~493 declared names contains no authoring.* action, and served-spec.lock.json contains none. documents.* is the V1 document lifecycle and does not provide an asset draft catalogue or intake queue.
findings.failure_scenario: An agent front end or UI calls authoring.intake to submit a document to the authoring queue, or authoring.publish to release a drafted asset: the registry returns no such action (404/unknown action), so the Authoring destination's intake, draft catalogue, review/publish and dependency-status flows have no HTTP or MCP surface and can only be faked through ad-hoc documents.* calls.
findings.acceptance: authoring.intake|draft|review|publish and authoring.assets are registered ActionSpecs with handlers, appear in served-spec.lock.json and the MCP manifest, and a registry test asserts the five names; or SPEC_V2 §10.4 is amended by owner decision naming the replacement family.

resolved_by.evidence: The five declared actions are registered ActionSpecs with handlers: authoring.intake, authoring.draft, authoring.review, authoring.publish and the authoring.assets read (registry 12/12 at 517 actions, 504 internal / 13 external; the served-spec lock carries all five operations and --check-lock is exit 0). The engine is migration 0066 (authoring_intake, authoring_asset, tenant RLS, one published row per kind/key) plus the store invariants: a draft is refused while a dependency is unpublished (then allowed once it publishes), a payload cannot carry approval_policy/effect_ceiling/grants/self_approval, review needs a HUMAN authoring.review gate naming the asset (pending and machine-only approvals refused), and publish needs a reviewed row. Proven by crates/actions/tests/authoring.rs (4 scenarios) and crates/store/tests/authoring.rs (5), with the parity suite (7/7) exercising all five over both transports.

findings.title: The kata.* family is not an action family; kata exists only as an unregistered process key
findings.problem: SPEC §10.4 declares kata.open|observe|analyse|propose|measure|adopt|propagate|close. No kata.* ActionSpec is registered. The implementation uses the string as a process-catalogue key: coach.escalate starts a process run with process_key 'kata.open' (coach.rs:780) and ops.incident names the same const (incidents.rs:64). There is no action to list a kata, read its Six Gests state, measure or adopt it, so the Improve destination's kata queue has no action surface.
findings.failure_scenario: coach.escalate opens a kata process run, but no kata.observe/measure/adopt action exists: an MCP client or the Improve screen cannot query the kata queue, record an observation/measurement or adopt the improvement, and the only way to advance it is the generic process_runs.start with a process key that must already be seeded. The systemic-improvement loop is not a discoverable API.
findings.acceptance: Either the eight kata verbs are registered as ActionSpecs (list/read state included) or SPEC §10.4 replaces the family with the process-key design and documents how observe/measure/adopt are expressed; a registry or process-catalogue test covers the chosen contract.

resolved_by.evidence: The kata family is now real: `kata.open|observe|analyse|propose|measure|adopt|propagate|close` plus the `kata.get|list` reads are registered ActionSpecs (registry 12/12 at 527, 504->514 internal; the served-spec lock carries all ten operations and --check-lock is 0), backed by migration 0067 (kata, kata_candidate, kata_measurement, kata_propagation). The Improve destination reads `kata.list` into its live queue. The five §12 T5 gates are proven through the action surface in crates/actions/tests/kata_gate.rs (9/9): unmeasurable kata refused, one open kata per signature, held-out split only, prediction before measurement, and a person other than the kata's opener OR MEASURER decides adoption — the measurer limb is pinned by crates/store/tests/kata.rs::the_kata_measurer_cannot_decide_its_adoption (store 9/9), which fails if that limb is removed. The seeded process key `kata.open` and the action now coexist (different registries).

findings.title: Four of the six declared analyse.* actions are missing
findings.problem: SPEC §10.4 and §10.4.1 declare analyse.site, analyse.app, analyse.video, analyse.brand, analyse.content and analyse.report as the evidence producers for gates. Only analyse.site (analysis/actions.rs:16) and analyse.video (analysis/video.rs:16) are registered; there is no analyse.app, analyse.brand, analyse.content or analyse.report in the registry, so four of the six measured subjects named by §10.4.1 cannot be analysed through the action surface.
findings.failure_scenario: A production or QC procedure carries a gate that names analyse.brand or analyse.content (the §10.4.1 example: scoring the subject of the project, not the system). The action does not exist, so the gate cannot produce its evidence row and the step fails at resolution; brand/content/application/report QC is impossible without out-of-band work, while §10.4.1 forbids building it inside metrics/evals.
findings.acceptance: analyse.app, analyse.brand, analyse.content and analyse.report are registered with schemas and handlers (or explicitly scoped out in SPEC §10.4 by owner decision), and a registry test asserts the final six-verb set.

findings.title: No spend budget gate: 429 tool_budget_exceeded is unimplemented and tool_call.cost is never written
findings.problem: §11.3 step 2 requires the broker to check the spend budget and fail with `429 tool_budget_exceeded`; §11.4's spend row requires 'budget check + ledger'; §11.8/§11.9 require cost per call. The broker performs only the effect-ceiling comparison (no budget read, no 429 branch anywhere in crates/), and writes the ledger row with `cost: None` unconditionally, so the column exists but is never populated and per-job 'tool-budget usage' cannot be computed.
findings.failure_scenario: A run whose binding permits `spend` calls `image_gen.generate` in a loop (image_gen is a first-wave toolkit). No budget counter is consulted before any of the calls; the destination produces paid renders on every iteration; every ledger row carries cost NULL, so the tenant's spend cannot be attributed and the gate that should have stopped at the first over-budget call never fires.
findings.acceptance: A spend-class tool call when the job's budget is exhausted returns `429 tool_budget_exceeded` before any network call; a successful spend call writes a non-null `cost` on its single `tool_call` row; a test drives `tools.call` for a spend tool under a zero budget and asserts the destination was never reached.

resolved_by.evidence: cargo test -p conveyor-actions --test tool_budget: 14 passed. A spend tool under a zero or exhausted budget is 429 tool_budget_exceeded with the stub's hit counter unchanged, and a successful spend call's single tool_call row carries the derived non-null cost.

findings.title: Write-verify is unenforced: no checks[]/verdict at call time and no publication gate for a write tool without verification
findings.problem: §11.3 states the two rules are 'not negotiable in the conveyor's registry': a write tool returns read-back `checks[]` and a `verdict`, and a write with no verification path cannot be published. The `tool` table has no verification declaration, `toolkits.publish` copies effect and schema from the action spec and inserts unconditionally, and the broker classifies the outcome from the HTTP status alone — it never inspects a `verdict` or `checks[]`. A write tool can therefore be published and called with no verification, and a 200 whose effect did not happen is ledgered `ok`.

evidence.quote: **Writes verify themselves.** A write tool returns read-back `checks[]` and a `verdict`; a write with no verification

findings.failure_scenario: A `write` tool (for example `coding.jobs.create`) is published with no checks declaration. findings.title: A paused tranche is a one-way door that freezes every project in it
findings.problem: `tranches.review` maps `pause` to state `paused` and a tranche can be reviewed only once. `projects.close` requires the project's tranche to be `authorised`, `in_review` or `closed`, so a paused tranche's projects can never close; the only remaining tranche actions are `tranches.update` (plan fields only), `tranches.retire` and `tranches.delete`, none of which resumes it. This was found by using the product: tranche 2 was paused on evidence with two projects open, and the close of S03 — whose Phase-G review is compliant and whose record is complete — was then refused `409 tranche_not_authorised`.
findings.failure_scenario: A tranche review that honestly records `pause` — the MSP answer when the exit criteria are not met — permanently prevents the very projects that could still meet them from closing. The programme has no way to resume short of deleting or retiring the tranche, so an honest pause converts a recoverable slip into a dead end.
findings.acceptance: Add a resume path (`tranches.resume` with an approving decision, or allow `tranches.review` to record a second dated review) and let a project close while its tranche is paused, with the closure recorded as in-flight work; a test proves a paused tranche can be resumed and that a compliant project can close in it.

resolved_by.evidence: spine_gates 14/14. `a_paused_tranche_resumes_only_with_its_approved_gate` refuses an unknown approval, a wrong gate, a pending gate, a wrong target and a machine-only decision (422 approval_missing each, the tranche left paused), then resumes under an approved HUMAN `tranche.resume` gate naming the tranche (200, state in_review), records the resume on the gate and refuses a second resume 409 tranche_not_paused. `a_compliant_project_closes_in_a_resumed_tranche` shows the freeze the finding names (every close record in place, still 409 closure_tranche_not_authorised) and the same close passing after the resume. `a_resumed_tranche_reviews_again_and_authorises_its_successor` proves the paused tranche still has its one review before the resume (409 tranche_already_reviewed) and that the resumed tranche records the second, dated review, whose `continue` closes it and authorises the next tranche.

findings.title: A ruling published without a text body is invisible to the pack, even when project-scoped
findings.problem: The pack renders only published documents whose body is stored as text and that belong to the programme: `list_published_outputs_tx` filters `body IS NOT NULL`, and the pack documents that as the publication decision. A decision created from bytes (object-backed, body null) is therefore published but absent from `docs/outputs.js` and `documents.preview` refuses it. R7 was first created projectless (excluded twice) and re-issued under PLATFORM (01a202a3) — still excluded, because its body is null (measured 2026-11-22: body null for 01a2029c and 01a202a3; the earlier delegation 01a2021d has a text body and is indexed). The re-issue was recorded as the fix; it is not one.
